fullData.title: Adding on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo wants to add $24$ and $13$ using the number line. He starts at $24$ and jumps forward by tens and ones to represent adding $13$. Look at the number line to see his starting position at $24$. How far does Leo need to jump in total to add $13$, and what number does he land on?

fullData.solutionStrategy: Break the added number into tens and ones to make forward jumps along the number line.

challenge.prompt: How is 13 written when broken apart into tens and ones?
challenge.rationale: The digit 1 represents one ten (10) and the digit 3 represents three ones (3), so 13 decomposes into 10 + 3.

annotations.steps: Split the number 13 into a ten and three ones.
annotations.strategy: I notice that breaking numbers by place value makes jumps on the number line much easier.
annotations.misconceptions: Students might mistakenly split 13 into 1 + 3 instead of recognizing the 1 represents a ten (10).
annotations.connections: This builds place-value understanding for mental math and addition strategies.
annotations.narrative: To add $13$, Leo needs to jump forward a total distance of $13$ units, which splits into $1$ jump of $10$ and $3$ jumps of $1$.

content.altText: A number line from 20 to 40 showing a starting point at 24, a jump of plus 10 to 34, and a jump of plus 3 to 37.

annotations.steps: Start at 24 on the number line, jump forward by 10 to reach 34, and then jump 3 more to land on 37.
annotations.strategy: I notice that breaking 13 into a ten and some ones makes jumping forward on the number line much easier.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This method connects counting on with place value, showing that adding numbers is like moving steps forward.
annotations.narrative: Starting at the Start point of $24$ in Figure 1, jumping forward $10$ reaches $34$, and jumping $3$ more reaches the End point at $37$, so Leo lands on $37$.

challenge.prompt: Leo starts at 24 and jumps forward by 10. What number does he land on?
challenge.rationale: Adding 10 to 24 gives 34, whereas counting the starting point 24 as the first move mistakenly leads to 33.

specs.title: Decompose the jump distance
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Understand how to break a two-digit addend into tens and ones for structured mental addition on a number line.
specs.seedNotes: Express the total jump of $13$ units as place-value components: $13 = 10 + 3$, representing $1$ jump of $10$ and $3$ jumps of $1$.

specs.title: Jump along the number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize addition as sequential forward hops along a number line from a given starting point.
specs.seedNotes: Show a number line starting at $24$, jumping forward $+10$ to land on $34$, then jumping $+3$ to reach the final position at $37$.
